rules.when: a worker runs on this runtime
rules.why: Pi renders a trust dialog before any composer; no key may answer it, so a card is raised and the endpoint is closed instead. A plain Enter submits. A Pi composer is a blank-separated pair of rows, and its status notice row below the composer is never absorbed as wrapped input. One Escape cancels the turn and leaves the composer empty, so no clear key and no arm signal are needed. The same table serves pi-signed, which is Pi under a signed launcher. Herdr binds one status authority to a pane, and Pi's lifecycle hooks outlive its process, so a replacement must resume the exact session that runtime recorded or its reports are ignored. The reference is used only when Pi itself registered it. While a turn runs the pane carries `esc to interrupt` with a rotating spinner word and an elapsed cell; idle it carries no elapsed cell. Busy is read from the lifecycle hooks, never from that footer.
